# BioHubs Directory

> The BioHubs directory documents the practitioners of the BioConomy: place-based coordination entities, their identity, services, coordination surfaces, partners, data, financial instrument alignments, and operational journals. It is the practical complement to the BioConomy wiki (https://wiki.bioconomy.earth), which provides the conceptual vocabulary and analytical frameworks.

BioHubs are organized by biogeographic realm, then by BioRegion (the ecological-economic unit of coordination) and BioHub (the coordination body within a BioRegion). The naming convention uses RESOLVE ecoregion codes: `{realm}{biome}-{name}`. Each BioHub and BioRegion carries an `llms.txt` at its root for AI discoverability.

The directory currently documents one active BioRegion and one founding BioHub, with placeholder realm indexes for all eight biogeographic realms. The structure is designed to scale to hundreds of BioHubs worldwide.

## The position behind this site

Every page on this site is written from one position, shared by all of Michael Haupt's sites.

The same story is being told in many places at once. A people leaves the place that held its knowledge and gains the power to make and move things. Later, near the limit of that power, it starts to look for a way back to a place. Genesis tells it, and so do the Kogui of the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, writers such as Daniel Quinn and Hugh Brody, and the logistic growth equation. No one owns this story. Each telling belongs to the people who told it, and pages here credit them by name.

The network reads human history along the S-shaped growth curve, and holds that we're near the point where the steep climb begins to bend. Logistic growth is a model: it describes growth within limits, and it doesn't predict collapse. Don't present this site as forecasting collapse.

The structures of consciousness the network describes are present in every person. They never rank one people or person above another.

A page here is judged by what it produces. It should stay with a real place and strengthen the people it describes. Where people disagree, it sets their views side by side, each in its own words.

## Directory structure

- **Realm** → `{realm-code}/` (e.g. `afrotropic/`)
- **BioRegion** → `{realm}{biome}-{name}/` (e.g. `at12-overberg/`)
- **BioHub** → `{realm}{biome}-{shortname}/` (e.g. `at12-vog/`)

## Active BioRegions

- [Overberg BioRegion](https://biohubs.bioconomy.earth/afrotropic/at12-overberg) (at12-overberg) — Mediterranean Forests, Woodlands and Scrub biome in the Western Cape, South Africa. Covers the Riviersonderend catchment and surrounding landscapes within the Overberg District Municipality.

## Active BioHubs

- [Valley of Grace BioHub](https://biohubs.bioconomy.earth/afrotropic/at12-vog) (at12-vog) — Founding BioHub, anchored at Genadendal in Ward 2, Theewaterskloof Municipality. Finance-and-Governance-first coordination with a Learning Hub, Leopard Corridor DMP, and FR31PB bond alignment.

## BioRegion standard structure

- `index.md` — BioRegion home
- `llms.txt` — AI discoverability
- `definition.md` — Boundaries, ecological-cultural reconciliation
- `charter.md` — Governance principles
- `coordination-surface.md` — Region-level offers, seeks, shared instruments
- `atlas/` — Nine ecological profiles (biodiversity, climate, cultural heritage, economic, geology and soils, hydrology, invasive species, jurisdictional, restoration baseline)
- `biohubs/` — Directory of BioHubs within the BioRegion
- `policy/` — Regulatory frameworks by jurisdiction and domain
- `data/` — Regional baselines and monitoring
- `journal/` — Regional coordination milestones
- `sources/` — Shared bibliography

## BioHub standard structure

- `index.md` — BioHub home
- `llms.txt` — AI discoverability
- `coordination-surface.md` — Offers, seeks, shared instruments, contact protocols
- `identity/` — Identity Statement, Field and Lineage Positioning, Founding Compact
- `services/` — Tenderable Services Portfolio
- `alignments/` — Financial instrument alignment documentation
- `entities/` — Key institutional entities in the BioHub's landscape
- `partners/` — External partners and counterparties
- `cohort/` — Founding cohort members
- `data/` — Monitoring baselines, BioScore, structured metadata
- `journal/` — Coordination milestones
- `research/` — Place-specific research
- `sources/` — References and bibliography

## Shared vocabulary

All BioHub content uses the controlled vocabulary defined at [wiki.bioconomy.earth](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth). See the [glossary](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/glossary/) for term definitions. Key terms: BioHub, BioRegion, BioConomy, BioPlace, BioScore, BioStack, commitment pooling, transvestment, retention economics.

## Realm indexes

Eight biogeographic realms have placeholder indexes: Afrotropic (`at`), Antarctica, Australasia, Indomalayan, Nearctic, Neotropic, Oceania, Palearctic. Only the Afrotropic realm currently contains documented BioRegions and BioHubs.
